skills.name: Slicing a cone
skills.wrong_turn: A parabola isn't one branch of a hyperbola. Hyperbola arms straighten toward asymptote lines; a parabola's never do.
skills.rule: A plane cuts a double cone in a circle, an ellipse, a parabola or a hyperbola.

skills.name: Parabola as focus & directrix
skills.wrong_turn: p is the distance from vertex to focus, not from focus to directrix. In x² = 12y, p = 3, and the directrix is 6 from the focus.
skills.rule: A parabola is the set of points equally far from a focus and a directrix.

skills.name: Parabola equations
skills.wrong_turn: The squared variable doesn't tell the direction of opening. (y − 1)² = 4(x + 2) opens right, not up.
skills.rule: (x−h)2=4p(y−k) opens up or down; (y−k)2=4p(x−h) opens right or left.

skills.name: Ellipse definition
skills.wrong_turn: The foci are inside the ellipse on its long axis, not on the curve. The constant sum is 2a, the major axis, not the distance between the foci.
skills.rule: An ellipse is the set of points whose distances to two foci add up to a constant 2a.

skills.name: Ellipse equations & graphs
skills.wrong_turn: The larger denominator sets the long direction, not which term comes first. x²/4 + y²/9 = 1 is tall, since 9 is under y.

skills.name: Ellipse foci
skills.wrong_turn: For an ellipse c² = a² − b², not a² + b². The foci are inside the curve, so c is less than a.
skills.rule: c2=a2−b2, and the foci lie c from the center along the major axis.

skills.name: Hyperbola definition
skills.wrong_turn: For a hyperbola c² = a² + b², not a² − b². The foci lie beyond the vertices, so c is bigger than a.
skills.rule: A hyperbola is the set of points whose distances to two foci differ by a constant 2a.

skills.name: Hyperbola graphs
skills.wrong_turn: The asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x only when x² comes first. For y²/a² − x²/b² = 1 they are y = ±(a/b)x.

skills.name: Classify conics

steps.b: signs of x² and y² terms

skills.wrong_turn: x² + y² = −4 fits the ellipse pattern but has no points at all. Complete the square before naming the curve.
skills.rule: For Ax2+Bxy+Cy2+Dx+Ey+F=0: B2−4AC<0 ellipse, =0 parabola, >0 hyperbola.

skills.name: Conics in the world
skills.wrong_turn: A dish's receiver sits at the focus, p from the vertex, not at the rim or level with the dish's depth.
skills.rule: Parabolas focus parallel rays, ellipses aim one focus at the other, hyperbolas locate by time differences.

skills.name: Systems with conics
skills.wrong_turn: Substituting and squaring can create extra answers. Check every solution in both original equations.
skills.rule: A line meets a conic at most twice, and two conics meet at most four times.
